nodes.label: Proof-Carrying Transactions report
nodes.rationale: Secondary synthesis with opaque citation markers; evidence cutoff September 6, 2026.

nodes.label: Proof-bearing transaction
nodes.rationale: A layered pattern; proof attachment alone does not establish history compliance.

nodes.label: Proof-carrying data
nodes.rationale: A prescribed compliance predicate covers the datum and the history that produced it.

nodes.label: Proof-carrying code
nodes.rationale: A producer supplies a formal safety certificate checked by a consumer.

nodes.label: Sequential incrementally verifiable computation
nodes.rationale: Sequential folding is a building block, not sufficient evidence of multi-party DAG PCD.

nodes.label: Recursive proof aggregation
nodes.rationale: Compression of proofs does not automatically compose their semantics or histories.

nodes.label: History compliance predicate
nodes.rationale: Every permitted transformation and predecessor relationship must satisfy the committed predicate.

nodes.label: Branching DAG composition
nodes.rationale: The outer relation must bind compatible predecessor outputs, policy and history.

nodes.label: Stateless recursive proving
nodes.rationale: Avoid persistent private prover-state dependencies between distrustful parties.

nodes.label: Private prover-state handoff
nodes.rationale: Required secret accumulator transfer creates custody, confidentiality and availability dependencies.

nodes.label: PCD-specific simulation extractability
nodes.rationale: Standalone soundness notions do not transfer automatically to adversarial recursive composition.

nodes.label: Typed PCT claim envelope
nodes.rationale: Authenticate typed claim descriptors and embedded or content-addressed evidence.

nodes.label: Signed intent and effect constraints
nodes.rationale: Bind authorized recipients, assets, gross spend, net delivery, fees, approvals and writes.

nodes.label: Contract and post-state invariants
nodes.rationale: Preservation claims require explicit specifications and preconditions.

nodes.label: Private authorization and eligibility
nodes.rationale: A credential predicate establishes an issuer-authenticated statement, with issuer and revocation assumptions.

nodes.label: Authenticated dependency footprint
nodes.rationale: Proving membership of declared accesses is weaker than proving the access set complete.

nodes.label: Execution validity
nodes.rationale: Committed machine execution does not establish intent, freshness, or external truth.

nodes.label: Execution-specific property
nodes.rationale: A property of one execution differs from a property of every execution.

nodes.label: Program-wide property
nodes.rationale: All-domain claims require an invariant or complete formal argument within a stated domain.

nodes.label: Current applicability
nodes.rationale: Canonical state freshness remains a separate acceptance condition.

nodes.label: External truth boundary
nodes.rationale: Authentication cannot establish real-world truth of an oracle or issuer assertion.

nodes.label: Ordinary ledger acceptance
nodes.rationale: Protocol validity and deterministic state transition remain part of PCT acceptance.

nodes.label: Versioned claim descriptor
nodes.rationale: Bind chain, protocol, transaction, intent, program, specification, verifier, state, effects, dependencies and validity interval.

nodes.label: Committed proof relation
nodes.rationale: A valid proof establishes existence of a witness for the specific committed relation under soundness assumptions.

nodes.label: Reusable formal certificate
nodes.rationale: A trusted kernel can check a precondition/program/postcondition theorem.

nodes.label: Proof-independent transaction core
nodes.rationale: Separate semantic authorization from proof bytes to avoid a circular transaction identifier.

nodes.label: Semantic authorization commitment
nodes.rationale: Sign the transaction core and semantic claim commitments before proof generation.

nodes.label: Final envelope commitment
nodes.rationale: Commit the completed envelope and evidence after semantic authorization.

nodes.label: Authenticated evidence sidecars
nodes.rationale: Content addressing must preserve mandatory claim bindings when evidence travels separately.

nodes.label: Fail-closed mandatory claims
nodes.rationale: Reject missing or unknown mandatory claims and unresolved dependencies.

nodes.label: Relying-party verifier authority
nodes.rationale: Transactions cannot select an arbitrary authoritative verifier or predicate.

nodes.label: Separate assurance axes
nodes.rationale: Soundness, binding, adequate specification, freshness and external assumptions must remain explicit.

nodes.label: Authenticated invariant base case
nodes.rationale: A global invariant requires an initial-state proof and coverage of every permitted transition.

nodes.label: Network-wide invariant coverage
nodes.rationale: Emergency, upgrade, mint and legacy bypasses invalidate a universal preservation claim.

nodes.label: Global consumption uniqueness
nodes.rationale: Local validity does not establish globally unique spending or canonical ordering.

nodes.label: UTxO and reference input binding
nodes.rationale: Exact output references aid freshness; consensus must establish they remain valid.

nodes.label: Account and storage freshness
nodes.rationale: Proofs may become stale while waiting for inclusion.

nodes.label: Object-version binding
nodes.rationale: Version references expose dependencies; shared-object order still requires coordination.

nodes.label: Shielded notes and nullifiers
nodes.rationale: Proofs can hide note data; consensus enforces nullifier uniqueness.

nodes.label: Complete effect relation
nodes.rationale: The relation must cover all observable effects, including fees, approvals, recipients and writes.

nodes.label: Human-to-policy intent capture
nodes.rationale: A compromised UI can display one policy and sign another.

nodes.label: Abstract resource bounds
nodes.rationale: Bound steps, memory, calls and output bytes; these are not wall-clock or liveness guarantees.

nodes.label: Complete read/write dependency sets
nodes.rationale: Implicit global state, code, fees, time and ordering can invalidate declared access completeness.

nodes.label: Noninterference and safe scheduling
nodes.rationale: Disjoint complete read/write sets provide a sufficient scheduling condition in the stated state model.

nodes.label: Accounting relative to explicit data
nodes.rationale: Collateral or balance proofs concern committed data, not complete liabilities or future solvency.

nodes.label: Oracle and issuer assumptions
nodes.rationale: Truth, freshness and coverage of external observations remain explicit assumptions.

nodes.label: Authenticated source-chain finality
nodes.rationale: Event membership alone does not establish inclusion in canonical finalized source history.

nodes.label: Solver-plan feasibility
nodes.rationale: A plan may prove feasibility in a declared state and intent.

nodes.label: Committed candidate-space optimality
nodes.rationale: Global best-price claims require authenticated market coverage and timing assumptions.

nodes.label: Data and witness availability
nodes.rationale: Validity proofs do not ensure required data exists for later users.

nodes.label: Network liveness and fairness
nodes.rationale: Future censorship resistance, fairness and progress require distributed assumptions.

nodes.label: Wallet or recipient certificate
nodes.rationale: Useful without protocol changes, but the ledger need not enforce the claim.

nodes.label: Application-enforced proof acceptance
nodes.rationale: A contract can reject actions lacking its required semantic evidence.

nodes.label: Optional execution accelerator
nodes.rationale: Ordinary execution may replace optional acceleration but must preserve the acceptance predicate.

nodes.label: Consensus-enforced envelope
nodes.rationale: Consensus-wide mandatory claim formats add protocol governance and verifier TCB obligations.

nodes.label: Batch or block recursive certificate
nodes.rationale: Amortization trades against latency, prover concentration and data availability.

nodes.label: Client-side proof-carrying history
nodes.rationale: Recipients verify provenance while the base ledger anchors uniqueness.

nodes.label: Transaction proof lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Intent, dependencies, proof generation, cheap checks, verification, inclusion and finality are distinct stages.

nodes.label: Exact-state proof
nodes.rationale: Expires when its state commitment changes.

nodes.label: Authenticated-fragment proof
nodes.rationale: Check individual current dependencies rather than the entire historical root.

nodes.label: Conditional transition proof
nodes.rationale: Current states satisfying the proved precondition may share a transition property.

nodes.label: Guard-and-path theorem reuse
nodes.rationale: Reuse requires current guard, path, program and semantics applicability.

nodes.label: Proof total-cost model
nodes.rationale: Measure W+P+A+R+NV against replicated direct execution NE.

nodes.label: State churn and reproving
nodes.rationale: Stale proofs create retry and reproof costs under contention.

nodes.label: Decision-grade performance benchmark
nodes.rationale: Use identical semantics and pinned hardware; measure tails, memory, witnesses, bytes and retries.

nodes.label: Prover concentration
nodes.rationale: Cheap validation may coexist with costly, concentrated production.

nodes.label: Mandatory safety has no silent fallback
nodes.rationale: Removing a required proof removes the claimed safety property.

nodes.label: End-to-end trusted computing base
nodes.rationale: Specification, compiler, proof implementation, encoding, policy, freshness and upgrades can each cause false acceptance.

nodes.label: Compiler and circuit correspondence
nodes.rationale: Underconstrained translation can invalidate source-level assurances.

nodes.label: Canonical statement serialization
nodes.rationale: All consumers must parse and hash the same statement.

nodes.label: Verifier versioning, revocation and migration
nodes.rationale: Agility requires relying-party authority and reviewed activation/revocation.

nodes.label: Invalid-proof denial of service
nodes.rationale: Perform bounded cheap admission checks before expensive verification; account for unauthenticated invalid proof cost.

nodes.label: Adversarial binding mutation suite
nodes.rationale: Mutate transaction, chain, code, key, specification, roots, effects, expiry, evidence and mandatory claims.

nodes.label: Valid execution with wrong recipient
nodes.rationale: A valid execution proof of paying Mallory must still fail Alice-signed intent.

nodes.label: Midnight semantic claim integration
nodes.rationale: Application proof semantics must bind higher-level claims and effects; direct Compact recursion is distinct from an extra recursive subsystem.

nodes.label: Predecessor and policy compatibility
nodes.rationale: Bind predecessor output roots to successor inputs and enforce an explicit policy combination rule.

nodes.label: Discharged recursive assumptions
nodes.rationale: Unresolved assumptions in composed evidence cannot count as unconditional acceptance.

nodes.label: Semantic-safety prototype
nodes.rationale: Compare ordinary signing, typed signing and independently checked signed effects.

nodes.label: Execution-efficiency prototype
nodes.rationale: Optional acceleration is justified by measured break-even, not proof size alone.

nodes.label: Three-party branching provenance prototype
nodes.rationale: Separate private witnesses and branch/join proof extension expose cross-party dependencies.

nodes.label: Investigation-phase decision gates
nodes.rationale: Freeze semantics, vectors, versions and baselines before assigning measured performance gates.

nodes.label: Engineering-phase decision gates
nodes.rationale: Add specialized claims, churn measurements, independent binding review, differential execution and safe revocation.

nodes.label: Deployment-phase decision gates
nodes.rationale: Decide enforcement per claim; consensus claims require independent implementations and tested migrations.

nodes.label: First-version exclusions
nodes.rationale: The report recommends against mandatory generic recursion and broad external truth or fairness guarantees; Moriarty requires an explicit adaptation.

nodes.label: Evidence and maturity ledger
nodes.rationale: Research constructions, reported benchmarks and deployed mechanisms establish different scopes.

nodes.label: Separate assurance axes
nodes.rationale: Soundness, binding, adequate specification, freshness and external assumptions must remain explicit.

nodes.label: Authenticated invariant base case
nodes.rationale: A global invariant requires an initial-state proof and coverage of every permitted transition.

nodes.label: Network-wide invariant coverage
nodes.rationale: Emergency, upgrade, mint and legacy bypasses invalidate a universal preservation claim.

nodes.label: Global consumption uniqueness
nodes.rationale: Local validity does not establish globally unique spending or canonical ordering.

nodes.label: UTxO and reference input binding
nodes.rationale: Exact output references aid freshness; consensus must establish they remain valid.

nodes.label: Account and storage freshness
nodes.rationale: Proofs may become stale while waiting for inclusion.

nodes.label: Object-version binding
nodes.rationale: Version references expose dependencies; shared-object order still requires coordination.

nodes.label: Shielded notes and nullifiers
nodes.rationale: Proofs can hide note data; consensus enforces nullifier uniqueness.

nodes.label: Complete effect relation
nodes.rationale: The relation must cover all observable effects, including fees, approvals, recipients and writes.

nodes.label: Human-to-policy intent capture
nodes.rationale: A compromised UI can display one policy and sign another.

nodes.label: Abstract resource bounds
nodes.rationale: Bound steps, memory, calls and output bytes; these are not wall-clock or liveness guarantees.

nodes.label: Complete read/write dependency sets
nodes.rationale: Implicit global state, code, fees, time and ordering can invalidate declared access completeness.

nodes.label: Noninterference and safe scheduling
nodes.rationale: Disjoint complete read/write sets provide a sufficient scheduling condition in the stated state model.

nodes.label: Accounting relative to explicit data
nodes.rationale: Collateral or balance proofs concern committed data, not complete liabilities or future solvency.

nodes.label: Oracle and issuer assumptions
nodes.rationale: Truth, freshness and coverage of external observations remain explicit assumptions.

nodes.label: Authenticated source-chain finality
nodes.rationale: Event membership alone does not establish inclusion in canonical finalized source history.

nodes.label: Solver-plan feasibility
nodes.rationale: A plan may prove feasibility in a declared state and intent.

nodes.label: Committed candidate-space optimality
nodes.rationale: Global best-price claims require authenticated market coverage and timing assumptions.

nodes.label: Data and witness availability
nodes.rationale: Validity proofs do not ensure required data exists for later users.

nodes.label: Network liveness and fairness
nodes.rationale: Future censorship resistance, fairness and progress require distributed assumptions.

nodes.label: Wallet or recipient certificate
nodes.rationale: Useful without protocol changes, but the ledger need not enforce the claim.

nodes.label: Application-enforced proof acceptance
nodes.rationale: A contract can reject actions lacking its required semantic evidence.

nodes.label: Optional execution accelerator

nodes.label: Consensus-enforced envelope

nodes.label: Batch or block recursive certificate

nodes.label: Client-side proof-carrying history
nodes.rationale: Recipients verify provenance while the base ledger anchors uniqueness.

nodes.label: Transaction proof lifecycle

nodes.label: Exact-state proof

nodes.label: Authenticated-fragment proof
nodes.rationale: Check individual current dependencies rather than the entire historical root.

nodes.label: Conditional transition proof

nodes.label: Guard-and-path theorem reuse

nodes.label: Proof total-cost model
nodes.rationale: Measure W+P+A+R+NV against replicated direct execution NE.

nodes.label: State churn and reproving

nodes.label: Decision-grade performance benchmark
nodes.rationale: Use identical semantics and pinned hardware; measure tails, memory, witnesses, bytes and retries.

nodes.label: Prover concentration
nodes.rationale: Cheap validation may coexist with costly, concentrated production.

nodes.label: End-to-end trusted computing base

nodes.label: Compiler and circuit correspondence

nodes.rationale: Current states satisfying the proved precondition may share a transition property.

nodes.label: Guard-and-path theorem reuse
nodes.rationale: Reuse requires current guard, path, program and semantics applicability.

nodes.label: Proof total-cost model
nodes.rationale: Measure W+P+A+R+NV against replicated direct execution NE.

nodes.label: State churn and reproving
nodes.rationale: Stale proofs create retry and reproof costs under contention.

nodes.label: Decision-grade performance benchmark
nodes.rationale: Use identical semantics and pinned hardware; measure tails, memory, witnesses, bytes and retries.

nodes.label: Prover concentration
nodes.rationale: Cheap validation may coexist with costly, concentrated production.

nodes.label: Mandatory safety has no silent fallback
nodes.rationale: Removing a required proof removes the claimed safety property.

nodes.label: End-to-end trusted computing base
nodes.rationale: Specification, compiler, proof implementation, encoding, policy, freshness and upgrades can each cause false acceptance.

nodes.label: Compiler and circuit correspondence
nodes.rationale: Underconstrained translation can invalidate source-level assurances.

nodes.label: Canonical statement serialization
nodes.rationale: All consumers must parse and hash the same statement.

nodes.label: Verifier versioning, revocation and migration
nodes.rationale: Agility requires relying-party authority and reviewed activation/revocation.

nodes.label: Invalid-proof denial of service
nodes.rationale: Perform bounded cheap admission checks before expensive verification; account for unauthenticated invalid proof cost.

nodes.label: Adversarial binding mutation suite
nodes.rationale: Mutate transaction, chain, code, key, specification, roots, effects, expiry, evidence and mandatory claims.

nodes.label: Valid execution with wrong recipient
nodes.rationale: A valid execution proof of paying Mallory must still fail Alice-signed intent.

nodes.label: Midnight semantic claim integration
nodes.rationale: Application proof semantics must bind higher-level claims and effects; direct Compact recursion is distinct from an extra recursive subsystem.

nodes.label: Predecessor and policy compatibility
nodes.rationale: Bind predecessor output roots to successor inputs and enforce an explicit policy combination rule.

nodes.label: Discharged recursive assumptions
nodes.rationale: Unresolved assumptions in composed evidence cannot count as unconditional acceptance.

nodes.label: Semantic-safety prototype
nodes.rationale: Compare ordinary signing, typed signing and independently checked signed effects.

nodes.label: Execution-efficiency prototype
nodes.rationale: Optional acceleration is justified by measured break-even, not proof size alone.

nodes.label: Three-party branching provenance prototype
nodes.rationale: Separate private witnesses and branch/join proof extension expose cross-party dependencies.

nodes.label: Investigation-phase decision gates
nodes.rationale: Freeze semantics, vectors, versions and baselines before assigning measured performance gates.

nodes.label: Engineering-phase decision gates
nodes.rationale: Add specialized claims, churn measurements, independent binding review, differential execution and safe revocation.

nodes.label: Deployment-phase decision gates
nodes.rationale: Decide enforcement per claim; consensus claims require independent implementations and tested migrations.

nodes.label: First-version exclusions
nodes.rationale: The report recommends against mandatory generic recursion and broad external truth or fairness guarantees; Moriarty requires an explicit adaptation.

nodes.label: Evidence and maturity ledger
nodes.rationale: Research constructions, reported benchmarks and deployed mechanisms establish different scopes.
